Bug_Title: Beans in "@Configuration" class should have different names
Bug_Details:
Naming conventions play a crucial role in maintaining code clarity and readability. The uniqueness of bean names in Spring configurations is vital
to the clarity and readability of the code. When two beans share the same name within a configuration, it is not obvious to the reader which bean is
being referred to. This leads to potential misunderstandings and errors.
Bug_Explanation: The code demonstrates a Spring configuration class with two beans defined with the same name 'myBean'. This violates the rule that beans in a '@Configuration' class should have different names, leading to potential confusion and runtime errors in bean management.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case calls the `showBug` method which attempts to simulate a conflict scenario caused by the duplicate bean names defined in the Spring configuration. The test fails because it expects a specific error message indicating a conflict within the configuration.
